yes_case.case: The closest historical episodes are the GST Council decisions to tax intermediary services provided by banks and NBFCs, and the imposition of GST on IT-enabled support services within financial conglomerates. In those past episodes, the Council moved decisively to plug input tax credit leakages where financial institutions were engaging external service providers. This episode differs primarily in the specific structural integration of co-lending partnerships between NBFCs and banks, which creates a more complex, highly visible trail of shared interest income and service fees. Unlike past broad-brush financial service exemptions, the current fiscal squeeze and the sheer volume of co-lending transactions provide a targeted revenue target that makes the 18% levy on NBFC-to-bank services uniquely compelling for the Council to formalize.

Unlike PSLCs, which were purely digital financial instruments traded without direct credit risk origination, or corporate guarantees which involved private intra-group arrangements, taxing NBFC-to-bank services directly impacts the structural viability of RBI-backed financial inclusion architectures. The distinct policy divergence between revenue-maximizing indirect tax authorities and credit-transmitting central banking mandates creates an institutional stalemate unique to this episode, preventing formal Council approval within the tight deadline.
